title: A name the captions split in half is still one name (R1002 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/oracle/caption-split-aliases.md` — **OD-6 / R1002**, evidence **BL-8**, whose measured recall test found the shipped table blind to `toma hawk`, `aor us master` and `air us elite`: silent losses in the corpus the whole product is built from.

New `alias_pattern` compiles one already-normalized surface form — an optional single space between adjacent characters **inside** a word, a **required** single space where the form itself has one.

**That asymmetry is the safety property, not a detail.** `aorus master` cannot match `aorusmaster`, because the alias's own space needs a real token boundary to land on; so with `compile_matcher`'s lookarounds a match always starts at a token start and ends at a token end, and `b650` is never found inside `theb650`.

`air us` for `aorus` is a mishearing no join recovers and stays the table's job, per R1002. Slice 3 adds it.

Still **one** compiled pattern, still longest-normalized-form-first with a stable sort, so R22's memory bound and R23's byte-identical rerun are untouched. `matched_form` stays `match.group(0)`, which is what makes the split spelling appear in the `aliases --check` report — R1002's stated measurement, which only measures anything if the form survives into it.

**The blind tests found a real gap in mine.** My sort-key test used `mag tomahawk` against `tomahawk`, which does **not** distinguish sorting on the normalized form's length from sorting on the pattern's — both orderings agree, so it would have passed against a wrong implementation. The blind author built a case that discriminates: `aa bb cc dd` (11 characters, 22 of pattern) against `aabbccddee` (10 characters, 28 of pattern), both matching at position 0.

It also tests "no lookarounds" behaviourally, pins the optional space as a single **literal** space (ruling out a `\s?` implementation), and declined to assert something I would have got wrong: `b 650 ex` legitimately **does** match B650, because the alias ends at a real token end. Only the fused `b650ex` is a reject.

757 passing.
